steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: AO6 Requirement: Accurate and effective punctuation isn't just about correctness - it's about using punctuation deliberately to create effects and control your reader's experience. | Tip: The colon acts like a spotlight, directing attention to what comes next. Use it to make important statements stand out. | Think of it this way: A semi-colon is stronger than a comma but weaker than a full stop. It shows ideas are connected but distinct. | Dash Tip: An em dash (—) is longer than a hyphen (-). In exams, you can use two hyphens (--) if you can't make an em dash.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Rewrite this sentence using a colon for emphasis: "She wanted one thing only, revenge." | Rewrite using a semi-colon: "The door slammed. She jumped." | Add a dash for dramatic effect: "He opened the box and saw something unexpected."
